title: Voucher Pair
statement:
A customer wants to pay a bill with exactly two vouchers. Each voucher has a
value in cents; the two must add up to the bill exactly.

Return the two positions, smaller first, of the vouchers to use. Every input has
exactly one pair that works, and a voucher may not be used twice.

**Example 1**

`voucher_pair([2, 7, 11, 15], 17)` returns `[0, 3]`: the vouchers worth 2 and
15 sum to 17.

**Example 2**

`voucher_pair([3, 3], 6)` returns `[0, 1]`.

**Constraints**

- `2 <= amounts.length <= 20000`
- `1 <= amounts[i] <= 2000000`
- `2 <= target <= 4000000`
guidelines: The classic two-sum. A nested loop passes everything but the perf case; the hashmap of value to position is what an experienced candidate reaches for straight away. Ask why the map is filled as you go rather than up front (the duplicate case).

test_cases.name: the pair is at the end
the pair is adjacent at the front
a decoy that would need the same voucher twice
